title: Count Good Nodes In Binary Tree
statement: A node is good if no node on the path from the root down to it has a bigger value. The root is always good. Given a binary tree, count its good nodes. The tree may be empty.

example.caption: 3 is good (the root). 1 is not (3 is above it). 4 is good. The lower 3 is good. The lower 1 is not (3 and 4 are above it).

idea.sentence: Walk down the tree and carry the biggest value seen on the path so far. A node is good if it is at least that big.

jargon.plain: The chain of nodes you pass going straight down from the root to a node. Only ancestors count, never siblings or cousins.
Depth-first search. Go all the way down one side, then come back and try the other side.

watch.inputHint: One argument: the tree as a level-order list, null for a missing child, e.g. [3,1,4,3,null,1,5]

compare.bruteLabel: Re-walk the path from the root for every node
compare.optimalLabel: Carry the max down while walking
compare.unit: comparisons (a tree that is a long chain)

rows.name: Re-check every path
rows.note: For each node, climb or walk the path to find the biggest value above it.

rows.name: Carry the max (DFS)
rows.note: Each node does one comparison. The call stack is as deep as the tree.

fast.takeaway: The biggest value on the path is all a node needs to know. Pass it down as one number and never look back up.

stages.title: Start with no bar
stages.note: Nothing is above the root, so the starting bar is the smallest possible number. The root always passes.

stages.title: Compare with the bar
stages.note: The node is good if its value is at least the biggest value above it. A tie counts.

stages.title: Raise the bar
stages.note: The children must beat the larger of the old bar and this node's value.

stages.title: Add up
stages.note: Count for this node, plus the good nodes on the left, plus the good nodes on the right. An empty spot counts 0.

edges.title: Empty tree
edges.why: There is no root to count. The empty spot returns 0.

edges.title: Equal values
edges.why: Good means no bigger value above it. A node equal to the bar is not beaten, so it is good.

edges.title: Falling chain
edges.why: Only the root is good. Every lower node has the 5 above it.

edges.title: Bigger than parent only
edges.why: 2 beats its parent 1 but not the root 3. Comparing with the parent alone would count it wrongly.

gotchas.text: Compare with the biggest value on the whole path, not with the parent. A node can beat its parent and still lose to a grandparent.
Use >= so that a tie is good. With > the equal-value tree [2,2,2] would give 1.
Pass the new bar to both children. Do not change one shared variable, or the left side's bar would leak into the right side.
-Infinity is a valid number in JavaScript, so it works as the 'nothing yet' bar. Starting from 0 would wrongly reject trees with only negative values.
Use math.MinInt as the starting bar. Writing 0 would reject a tree whose values are all negative.

recap.key: Pass the biggest value on the path as an argument. A node is good when it is at least that big.
recap.complexity: Time O(n). Space O(h) for the call stack.
